hero.title: Big taste for a
hero.lede: A capability-oriented control plane for self-hosted AI agents—designed from the start for Raspberry Pi, your own hardware, and authority you can understand.
hero.installCommand: git clone https://github.com/dekopon-agents/dekopon.git && cd dekopon && cargo install --locked --path crates/dekopon
hero.caveat: v0.1.0 is a local catalog CLI. It makes no model calls and executes no external effects.

title: Everything it needs.
Nothing it doesn’t.
pillars.intro: Dekopon starts with the constraints of hardware you can hold in one hand. Its architecture stays legible, modular, and economical as your agents grow.

items.title: Designed for a small footprint.
items.body: A synchronous Rust CLI today. No required cloud control plane, no idle runtime stack, and no heavyweight dependency without tested behavior that earns it.

items.title: Designed for capabilities.
items.body: Agents receive a vocabulary of narrow operations—not a bag of credentials. Proposing a capability never grants the process authority to execute it.

items.title: Designed for customizability.
items.body: Compose typed resources now; add narrow provider components as the runtime matures. Transport-independent boundaries keep your configuration portable.

items.title: Designed for observability.
items.body: Proposal, trusted identity, policy decision, bounded execution, result, and evidence are designed to remain linked under one trace.

status.title: Start with what is real.
status.intro: Dekopon draws a bright line between code you can run today and constraints accepted for the system ahead. A roadmap is not an implementation claim.

current.label: Current · v0.1.0
current.title: A small, deterministic local control path.
current.body: One operator-selected catalog goes through strict decoding, typed validation, resource reads, and predictable rendering.
points: Table, JSON, YAML, wide, and name output

direction.label: Committed direction
direction.title: Brokered execution with narrow authority.
direction.body: The target architecture separates unprivileged orchestration from the only process allowed to turn proposals into constrained effects.
direction.note: These components are design constraints, not shipped features.

authority.title: A model may propose.
authority.intro: Success does not mean making a model trustworthy. It means containing an untrusted model in a system where every unit of authority is narrow, attributable, reviewable, and revocable.

nodes.title: Proposal
nodes.body: Intent and arguments from a model, repository, or tool payload.

nodes.title: Broker
nodes.body: Authenticates identity, evaluates policy, and binds constraints to a receipt.

nodes.title: Provider
nodes.body: Executes one narrow operation with broker-held credentials and enforced limits.

nodes.title: Evidence
nodes.body: Links identity, proposal, decision, policy revision, effect, and result.

invariants.title: Explicit and narrow
invariants.body: A read capability never implies write authority. Every external write gets its own name.

invariants.title: Identity from trust
invariants.body: Actor identity comes from authenticated infrastructure, never model text or repository content.

invariants.title: Credentials contained
invariants.body: Secrets stay behind the broker boundary—out of prompts, authored resources, evidence, and logs.

invariants.title: Authorization bound
invariants.body: The proposal, decision, execution limits, and receipt travel as one constrained grant.

resources.title: Declare capabilities in the open.
resources.intro: Compact, Kubernetes-inspired resources make an agent’s proposed authority inspectable. Unknown fields fail early. Names and references are validated before they enter the catalog.

points.label: api
points.title: Versioned on the wire
points.body: with explicit kinds and strict alpha schemas.

points.label: key
points.title: Symbolic credential references
points.body: keep real secrets out of authored resources.

points.label: sort
points.title: Deterministic ordering
points.body: keeps output stable for people and automation.

resources.yaml:
apiVersion: dekopon.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Agent
metadata:
  name: reviewer
spec:
  description: Reviews pull requests
  capabilities:
    - github.pull-request.read
    - github.pull-request.comment
status: Ready
resources.terminal:
$ dekopon get agents -o wide

NAME       ENABLED   CAPABILITIES   STATUS
reviewer   true      2              Ready
snooper    false     1              Disabled

$ dekopon validate
✓ configuration is valid

architecture.title: Coordination is not authority.
architecture.intro: The operator, orchestrator, broker, and provider each have one legible job. A process never gains effect authority merely because it coordinates a task.

current.title: Human control CLI
current.body: Parse commands, read typed resources, render results.

components.title: Unprivileged orchestrator
components.body: Model interaction, context, memory, and task coordination.

components.title: Authority broker
components.body: Authentication, policy, credentials, execution, and evidence.

components.title: Narrow provider
components.body: A fresh, bounded store for one integration operation.

roadmap.title: Earn authority one boundary at a time.
roadmap.intro: Each milestone proves the shape of the next. Heavy machinery arrives only with meaningful, tested behavior—not as an empty promise in the dependency graph.

items.title: Local control CLI
items.body: Typed catalog, strict validation, deterministic reads, and explicit invocation states.

items.title: Authenticated daemon protocol
items.body: An unprivileged task service with no external-write authority.

items.title: Separate broker prototype
items.body: Policy decisions, constrained receipts, evidence, and append-only audit records.

items.title: One read-only provider
items.body: A meaningful end-to-end integration before any external write is introduced.

items.title: Policy + Wasm isolation
items.body: Cedar after inputs stabilize; Wasmtime with a fresh constrained store per invocation.

closing.title: Build agents that can act.
closing.body: Dekopon is early, intentionally small, and open to careful contributors.
